Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: Comprehensive district-wide inventory including detailed site plans, building sizes, ages, and specialized spaces; robust condition assessment covering all major systems with multiple data sources; connects condition data to student outcomes and integrates short- and long-term needs into capital planning (Chapters 2, 5; Facility Assessment and Grading; Master Planning).

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: Provides detailed enrollment projections over 10 years with methodology explained; includes capacity utilization data by site and grade; links enrollment projections to specific facility actions including new construction, reconfiguration, and adaptive uses; considers demographic trends and housing patterns (Chapters 1, 5; Enrollment Analysis; Master Planning).

Educational Alignment.justification: Educational alignment is a core organizing principle; detailed educational specifications for all school levels; clear integration of district mission, instructional priorities, and facilities planning; facility projects directly respond to educational goals including STEM, CTE, special education, and collaborative learning (Chapter 4; Educational Specifications).

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: District-wide data on outdoor spaces including playfields, gardens, and hard courts; detailed strategies for campus greening such as stormwater retention, permeable paving, and community gardens; frames outdoor spaces as climate resilience strategies; includes outdoor learning and environmental literacy (Chapters 2, 5; Facilities Assessment; Master Planning).

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: Plan addresses climate impacts such as stormwater management and heat mitigation with detailed strategies including stormwater retention systems and permeable paving; climate readiness is a priority and theme in planning and design; however, comprehensive multi-risk district-wide climate risk assessment is limited (Chapters 2, 5; Facilities Assessment; Master Planning).

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: Energy resilience and efficiency are core parts of the plan; includes data on energy use and strategies for reduction; references state requirements (Title 24, Zero Net Energy goals); plans for electrification, renewable integration, and resilience strategies such as solar and microgrids; connects energy improvements to climate-related disruptions (Chapter 2; Facilities Assessment; Master Planning).

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: Comprehensive capital strategy with detailed cost estimates, prioritization criteria, and multiple funding strategies including bonds, state programs, and alternative financing; includes escalation assumptions, contingencies, and long-term financial sustainability considerations; aligns financial capacity with educational priorities and facility needs (Chapter 5; Implementation; Funding Opportunities).
